# Best waterproof Bluetooth speakers for the pool or beach

**My top pick is the JBL Charge 6.** What Hi-Fi, BestProducts, and iTechGuides all rank it best overall. It's rated IP68 (dust-tight, built for immersion), has 20 hours of battery (up to 28 with Playtime Boost), puts out 40W, and can charge your phone. It runs about $130 at Walmart to $150 at Amazon.
- [Buy links in What Hi-Fi's review](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart)
- [BestProducts' review](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/), which listed it at $150 (25% off)

## Other picks by need

| Need | Speaker | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Loud pool party | **JBL Boombox 4** | RTINGS' top waterproof pick. It's built for long immersion, floats, and has 40+ hours of battery. Sound is directional, so it's best when you're in front of it. Price wasn't listed. [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth) |
| Even sound all around | **Ultimate Ears Epicboom** | Tom's Guide's best overall and RTINGS' best mid-range. It's IP67 with 360° sound, floats, and has about 15 hours of battery. [Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers) |
| Budget | **Ultimate Ears Wonderboom 4** | IP67, floats, 14 hours of battery, and about $65–80. It's softball-sized and quieter than the bigger models. [BestProducts](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/) |
| Cheapest or pocket-size | **JBL Go 5** | IP67, about $40, with 8 hours of battery. [What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart) |
| Easy to carry to the beach | **JBL Grip** | Good Housekeeping's best overall. It's IP68, can-shaped, under a pound, about $100, and has 12 hours of battery. [Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/) |
| Big, floating party speaker | **Soundcore Boom 2 Plus** | 100W, floats, IPX7, and up to 20 hours of battery at half volume. It's heavy at 3.8 kg. The listed price is $249.99, or $200 with code AFSC20, which the source says it tested at Soundcore's cart. [Buy at Soundcore](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-boom-2-plus) (affiliate link) |

Aside from the Soundcore link, the links above go to the review pages, which have current retailer buy buttons. I can't confirm exact product-page URLs or live prices from the search results, so check the price at checkout.

## Tips
- **Check the rating.** Look for IP67 or higher, or IPX7 at minimum. For sand, the first digit matters too: IP6X means dust-tight, while IPX7 says nothing about dust. Keep an IPX7 speaker on a towel.
- **Rinse after use.** RTINGS notes that IP ratings don't cover salt or chlorine damage, so rinse with fresh water, and some manuals advise against beach use. Close the charging-port flap and dry the speaker fully before charging. ([RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth))
- **Think about floating.** A speaker that floats is easier to recover if it falls in the pool. The Boombox 4, Epicboom, Wonderboom 4, and Boom 2 Plus all float.

If you tell me your budget and whether you want it for a small group or a bigger party, I can narrow this down to one.
